summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 3.14/154)

data.turoyo: Kətwolən ḥmoro, b qḏole ṣlibo mʕalqo, bu mḥoyo mgargəšiwole w muḥanwole baḥ ḥaṭroṯo.
data.translation: They had a donkey, with a cross hung on its neck; they were dragging it along with blows and striking it with sticks.

rationale: New Infectum-wa box; overt donkey antecedent, plural agent and object suffix.

data.turoyo: <...> B ḥal naxoš", — omər, — "mgargašli ruḥi l gawa di gamiye w annaqqa rawəxno ono ste, mobeleli bu darbo, d kəzzeyo. <...>
data.translation: <...> Mit Mühe und Not kletterte ich in das Schiffhinein und bestieg es, und er nahm mich mit auf den Weg, den er fuhr.

rationale: Fills Preterit with first-person self-directed hauling and explicit endpoint.

data.turoyo: Omər: "Me tamo mgargašlan ruḥayna, hul d aṯina li walaye d Ṣṭambəl.
data.translation: Von dort schlugen wir uns durch bis wir nach der Stadt Stambul kamen.

rationale: Fills Preterit with first-person plural reflexive and extended difficult travel.

data.turoyo: U kuruk rawəx. Rawəx li kačke, mədla lu hafṣoro du səsyayḏe w mgargašla annaqqa, d məblole se Be Qara Taždin.
data.translation: Der Junge saß auf. Er saß auf, und das Mädchen faßte den Halfter seines Pferdes und zog es hinter sich her, um ihn zum Hause Kara Tadschdins zu bringen.

rationale: Fills Preterit with feminine agent and horse patient, complementing the inherited lion context.

data.turoyo: L Hetim mədle lak kazəkat di ḥurmayḏe, mgargšole, mdawdḥole mi qalʕo w laltaḥ.
data.translation: Da packte Hatim seine Frau an den Zöpfen und zerrte sie, ließ sie herunter von der Burg.

rationale: Fills Preterit to five with overt l-marked agent and feminine object-bearing mgargšole.

summary: Ordinary dragging and explicit self-directed motion retain the same transitive frame. ruḥi/ruḥayna/ruḥux is an object and does not make the verb Detransitive.
The Preterit shows -li, -lan and feminine-agent -la; mgargšole combines feminine object with masculine-agent -le. Paths may be bəṯre ruḥa, l gawa di gamiye or li walaye.
The glossary files this quadriliteral as I. Morphological descriptions saying Q do not justify changing that inherited stem label.
The supplied entry already contains the plank Imperativ and halter Infectum. The travel clauses add context, but no new light-verb idiom is established.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce has no edition translation. English quotations below retain the supplied project machine translation and are marked as such; sense decisions rest on the Turoyo. Where available, round-1 proposals are retained in the human layout and counts, and are not resubmitted in this JSON.
Both occurrences retain inherited I.1 dragging. The quadriliteral shape does not authorise relabelling the glossary’s I as Q.
Jan supplies habitual/ongoing past mgargəšiwole, a box not proposed in round 1. Donkey versus human patients do not create a separate meaning.
The Preterit thin-cell claim used the original one-example count; after round 1 there are five. No new sense, idiom or correction of existing material is required.
Is mgargašlan ruḥayna at 63/321 conventionalized as difficult travel, or a productive extension of hauling oneself? The broad existing sense is retained.
Explicit ruḥ- object allows difficult self-motion and onward travel; this extends the already attested Imperativ reflexive use.
